entries.evidence: The V2 engine (sub-model 8840 - step4b.ldr, built at the book's step 9) has two connecting rods p117 and p118 2852 on the crankshaft's pin, and two pistons p120 and p121 2851 in their cylinders. The file draws each rod's ball 2.0 and 2.2 LDU off its cylinder's axis and each piston 3.4 and 3.7 LDU above its rod's ball, 4.3 and 4.6 LDU apart in all, so no rod is read as holding its piston: the crank and rods turn, and the pistons stay still (function 2). A rod's ball sits in its piston, as built: turned a few degrees on the crankshaft's pin, in its own plane, each rod's ball lies on its cylinder's axis, and each piston, slid down its cylinder, seats on it.
